newsitem.title: JAPAN: GOLF-TESHIMA KEEPS NORMAN AT BAY.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TESHIMA KEEPS NORMAN AT BAY.

text.p: Japan's Taichi Teshima equalled the course record of 62 in the opening round of the $1 million Chunichi Crowns tournament on Thursday.
He kept the overseas contingent headed by Greg Norman at bay with ease on the Nagoya course as he opened up a four-shot lead in his bid for a first Tour success..
Teshima's eight-under-par round comprised nine birdies -- five in succession from the sixth hole -- and a solitary bogey.
Norman, New Zealander David Smail and two Japanese shared second place.

World number one Norman, enjoying clear, sunny conditions on fairways that favoured his long drives, recorded seven birdies. But he also dropped shots at three holes as his putting occasionally let him down.
Teshima matched the course best set by Australian Anthony Gilligan and Japan's Haruo Yasuda in 1995 and 1970 respectively.
Local favourite Masashi Ozaki, going for his third straight title here, shot a 67 along with his younger brother Tateo and seven others.
American Craig Stadler was one stroke further back in the chase for the $250,000 first prize..
